newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish consortium buys Lodz cigarette plant.
newsitem.headline: Polish consortium buys Lodz cigarette plant.

text.p: A consortium of two Polish firms, Merkury SA and Granex SC, on September 30 bought a 79.99 percent stake in the Lodzka Wytwornia Papierosow SA cigarette plant for 102,816 zlotys, the privatisation ministry said.
It said in a statement the consortium also took over Lodz's 6.5 million zloty debt, agreed to provide credit for up to two million zlotys and equipment worth more than $2 million.

Lodz's employees would be offered 15 percent of the shares and the five percent would be put aside for reprivatisation claims. The state will retain one golden share which would enable it to block the liquidation of the firm.
The consortium will keep Lodz's 170 jobs for 15 months and raise wages by 60 zlotys. The average wage in Lodz is 665 zlotys. The firm produces mainly cheap "Klubowe" and "Popularne" brands.

Lodz's share capital is 6.12 million zlotys divided into 612,000 shares of a nominal value of 10 zlotys each. It is the smallest of Poland's cigaretter companies with its production accounting for about 1.8 percent of Poland's total output.

Poland has so far sold four tobacco companies in the cities of Augustow, Radom, Krakow and Poznan. The privatisation of the industry will be concluded with the sale of another plant in Radom and one in Lublin.
